title: Choose the visual world for the LNYQ landing page
question: The roll assigned The Pit Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Pit Board
options.lineage: open-outcry trading pits and the chalked quotation boards behind them
options.thesis: The landing page is the price board itself: every devnet market chalked as a ruled row with its live best bid, depth and state, and the order book is the hero because it is the product.
options.viewport: A full-bleed slate board. Top rail: LNYQ chalked in tall industrial caps with the one-line hook. Below it the board proper: thirteen ruled rows, one per devnet market, symbol, best bid, resting depth, status, read live from the gateway and updating as orders land. A real candle chart drawn in chalk for the market with fills; where no fills exist yet it draws the live bid ladder as depth and says so. Launch app and Request access hang as plaques on the board edge.
options.risk: Chalk lettering tips into novelty if the display face is cute; the board must be ruled and numbered like a real price board, not a cafe menu.

raised.raise: The live price tape is the page's one unbroken line with a now marker that never wraps.
One market per full-width ruled row, every number tabular and registered to the same columns.
Each market keeps one chalk colour everywhere it appears on the page.
Control states are drawn, not styled: pressed is filled chalk, disabled is a rubbed-out line.

options.label: The Dojima Ledger
options.lineage: the Dojima rice exchange, Osaka, where Homma drew the first candlestick charts
options.thesis: The candle chart goes home: a tall ledger sheet in sumi ink with vermilion closes, the live devnet market drawn the way price was first drawn.
options.viewport: One tall ledger sheet. The first column is the live candle chart in ink; the facing columns are the markets as ledger lines with best bid and depth; the LNYQ seal in vermilion is the primary action.
options.risk: The most familiar strong direction for a chart-led product, and light paper is the opposite of what this audience's screens look like at night.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The order book ladder as a visible construction grid; the headline assembles from the same cells the price levels sit in.
options.viewport: Faint grid over the whole sheet; LNYQ built cell by cell at the top; the live book snapped to the grid below.
options.case: Holds product clarity: a grid is an honest home for a price ladder. Loses audience identification: traders do not read Dutch specimen posters.
options.risk: Reads as a design-school exercise unless the grid carries live numbers.

options.label: Risograph Zine Cover
options.thesis: Bids in one ink, asks in the other, the spread as the third colour where they overlap.
options.viewport: Pink bids over blue asks, misregistered on purpose; the overlap is the live spread.
options.case: Holds audience identification for the collectible-culture side of LNYQ. Loses clarity: two misregistered inks fight tabular numbers.
options.risk: Numbers become hard to read exactly where the product needs them exact.

options.label: Blacksmith Scale Shower
options.case: Traders do not identify with a forge, and a blow-per-row cannot carry a two-sided book.
options.kept: One event per full-width ruled row with measured state registered.

options.label: Sleeping City Fold
options.case: No trader or creator sees their world in a dreaming city, and folds hide numbers.
options.kept: Each district keeps its own tint: one colour per market everywhere.

options.label: Drum Machine Step Row
options.case: A loop of sixteen steps has no bid and no ask; the mechanism does not fit.
options.kept: One unbroken line that never wraps, with a chase light that shows where now is.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.case: Nostalgia for a desktop this audience never used, and dither erases fine numerals.
options.kept: Unambiguous drawn states: pressed inverts, disabled dims.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark crypto landing: split hero with copy left and product right, badge row, three product cards, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline over subcopy and two buttons, the terminal screenshot beside it, cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other venue by design.
